# Kingboard Laminates Holdings (1888.HK) — Forensic Dossier

*A deep dive on the business, management, and the setup, for the committee. Prepared 2026-07-17. Prices in Hong Kong dollars (HK$).*

**A note on sources.** No verbatim earnings-call transcript was available for this name (Hong Kong industrial issuers rarely host English-language calls, and none was bundled). This dossier is therefore built from the hard financials in our screener, the company's dated results announcements and profit alerts, its published price-increase notices, the June 2026 controlling-shareholder share sale, and sell-side commentary — all cross-checked against live market data. Where I could not source a management quote, I say so rather than invent one.

Kingboard Laminates is the world's largest maker of copper-clad laminate (CCL) — the copper-and-glass-fibre sheet that is the base material for printed circuit boards (PCBs). It has held that number-one share for roughly two decades. It also makes the upstream feed for CCL (glass yarn, glass fabric, copper foil, epoxy resin, bleached kraft paper) and runs small property and investment portfolios. It is the listed laminates arm of the Kingboard group; the parent, Kingboard Holdings (0148.HK), is the controlling shareholder.

---

## 1. Narrative Arc

The story has swung from "cyclical laggard" to "AI-infrastructure shortage winner" in about eighteen months, and the share price has swung far harder than the business.

- **2021 peak, then a deep trough.** Revenue peaked at HK$28.8B in 2021 with net income of HK$6.78B and earnings per share of HK$2.17. The cycle then broke: revenue fell to HK$16.75B by 2023 and earnings per share collapsed to HK$0.29 — a roughly 87% earnings decline peak-to-trough. This is the single most important fact about the company: it is deeply cyclical, and the last down-leg was brutal.
- **2024–2025 recovery.** Revenue re-based higher (HK$18.54B in 2024, HK$20.4B in 2025, up about 10%) and earnings inflected sharply — 2025 net profit rose about 85% to roughly HK$2.49B on an underlying basis (reported earnings per share HK$0.78). Management framed the recovery around demand for high-frequency, high-speed, low-loss laminates used in artificial-intelligence servers and 5G/6G equipment, plus electric and smart vehicles.
- **2026 pricing super-cycle.** The narrative escalated into a genuine shortage story. Kingboard has pushed through four price-increase notices since April 2026 (cumulatively about 53%), the latest on 6 July 2026 (up to 15% on FR-4 and prepreg). Industry data shows standard FR-4 laminate rising from about 70 yuan a sheet in July 2025 to about 260 yuan by June 2026 — more than 270% in a year — while premium AI-grade materials (so-called M8/M9) sell at seven to fifteen times ordinary FR-4.

The growth driver that was quietly dropped from the old story — commodity FR-4 oversupply and price wars — has been replaced by its mirror image: a supply-constrained, price-led boom. What has *not* changed is that this is the same cyclical commodity-materials business; only its position in the cycle has.

## 2. Claims vs Financials (forensic)

| Management claim | The financial evidence | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| Demand is strong across AI, 5G/6G and vehicles | Laminate volume 116M sheets in 2025 (+6%); revenue +10%; division EBITDA +22% to HK$3,676.6M | Matches — but note volume grew only 6%; most of the profit jump is **price/mix, not units** |
| Profit is surging | 2025 net profit ~HK$2.49B (+85%); the Feb 2026 profit alert guided +80% and was met | Verified — management guided and delivered |
| Pricing power is real | Four hikes since April 2026, cumulative ~53%; FR-4 spot +270% year-on-year | Verified from published notices and industry data |
| Balance sheet is sound | Net gearing ~16%; net debt only ~HK$1.75B against ~HK$17B equity; Altman-Z solvency score 15.2; Piotroski quality 7/9 | Verified — genuinely conservative financing |

Where the story is *richer than the numbers justify*: the market has treated a spot-price spike as durable structural growth. The 6% volume growth tells you the unit demand, while healthy, is not the 10x-stock story — the price line is doing the heavy lifting, and price is the most reversible part of a cyclical.

One data-quality flag for the committee: our screener's model fair values for this name (a discounted-cash-flow value near HK$0.3, a Buffett value near HK$1.1, and "margin of safety −100%" on every method) are broken outputs, not signals. They were computed off an annual free-cash-flow figure that rounded to roughly zero (the "P/FCF 0.0x" and "FCF −0.4%" lines), which makes any cash-flow-discount model divide by nothing. The trailing-twelve-month free cash flow is actually positive at about HK$1.86B. So ignore the "deep value, −100% margin of safety" label — it is an artifact, and the real picture is the opposite of cheap.

## 3. Tone & Confidence Trajectory

**Trajectory: strengthening (operationally).** With no call transcript, I read tone from actions rather than words, and the actions are confident: four price hikes in a quarter, HK$1.3B of new-capacity investment in 2025, a dividend raised 25% plus a special dividend (final 25.0 cents plus special 28.0 cents), and a controlling shareholder willing to expand aggressively. This is offensive, growth-and-investment posture, not defensive cost-cutting. The business is clearly in its strong half-cycle.

The caution flag is that the loudest confidence signal — repeated price increases — is also the most cycle-sensitive. Confidence expressed through pricing power evaporates the moment the shortage does.

## 4. Guidance Credibility

**Reliability: high.** The one hard, dated commitment we can check — the 23 February 2026 profit alert guiding full-year net profit up about 80% to top HK$2.39B — was delivered and slightly beaten (about HK$2.49B underlying). Dividends have been raised in line with earnings. There is no sandbagging or over-promising pattern in the evidence available. Management says what it will earn and earns it. The credibility question is not honesty; it is durability.

## 5. Analyst Pressure Points

The sell-side is uniformly bullish and, in my view, is the pressure point rather than the check on it. The consensus twelve-month target sits around HK$59.58 (high HK$130, low HK$25.3), with five buy ratings and no sells. Citi (8 June 2026) carries a buy at HK$80 and projects a 46% compound annual earnings growth rate through 2028. The analysts are extrapolating the current price super-cycle years forward. The topic they are *not* pressing management on is the one that matters: what happens to earnings when spot laminate prices — up 270% in a year — normalise as the industry's new capacity (Kingboard's own, plus the wider industry's) comes online. That is the unasked question.

## 6. Red Flags / Green Flags

**Green flags**
- 🟢 Real, verifiable pricing power right now, in a genuinely tight high-end market where Kingboard is the scale leader.
- 🟢 Conservative balance sheet (net gearing ~16%, net debt ~HK$1.75B) — the company can survive a down-cycle, which it has done before.
- 🟢 Guidance delivered (the February profit alert was met), and a rising, well-covered dividend.

**Red flags**
- 🔴 **The controlling shareholder sold near the top.** On 17 June 2026 the parent, Kingboard Holdings, placed 155 million Laminates shares at HK$76 — an 11.5% discount to the then-HK$85.90 price — raising about US$1.5B (HK$11.77B) to fund group capacity. The best-informed insider chose to monetise a slug of stock in the mid-HK$80s. The shares now trade at HK$41.98, roughly half that placement price. That is both an overhang (more freely floating stock) and a valuation tell.
- 🔴 **Peak-cycle earnings, cyclical business.** Spot FR-4 at +270% is not a sustainable run-rate; the last cycle saw earnings per share fall 87% from peak.
- 🔴 **The share price is unwinding violently.** From a 52-week high of HK$107.20 the stock has fallen to HK$41.98 — down about 61% — and dropped roughly 14% on 17 July alone, part of a broad Hong Kong AI-hardware sell-off (Nvidia's "Kyber" rack reportedly pushed to 2028; Meta reportedly weighing selling computing capacity, feeding oversupply fears; an overnight Nasdaq drop of over 6%).

## 7. Hidden Signals

- **Volume versus price.** The quiet tell in the 2025 numbers is that units grew 6% while profit grew 85%. The franchise is real, but the earnings surge is overwhelmingly a pricing event — which is exactly the line item that mean-reverts.
- **Capacity is the industry's answer to shortage.** Kingboard invested HK$1.3B in 2025 capacity and the parent raised US$1.5B expressly to add PCB capacity. When a shortage is this profitable, the whole industry builds — and the cure for high prices is high prices. The capital-allocation signal (build aggressively into the boom) is rational for the company but bearish for the durability of the pricing that supports today's valuation.
- **Investment segment noise.** A HK$503.5M fair-value gain on equity holdings flattered 2025's result (versus a HK$79.3M loss in 2024). This is non-operating and can reverse; strip it out when normalising earnings.

## 8. Capital-Allocation Verdict (for the director)

**Classification: strengthening — but into a cyclical peak.** The single most important thing to weigh before sizing is this: you are being asked to pay a growth-stock multiple (roughly 30 times or more on forward earnings, over 50 times trailing reported earnings) for a deeply cyclical commodity-materials company at what looks like the top of a once-in-a-cycle price spike — and the controlling shareholder has just sold into that spike. The "deep value / fresh crash" tag is misleading: the crash is real, but the valuation is not cheap.

**Economic moat: narrow.** The moat type is scale-cost leadership (world's largest CCL maker) plus a real but partial qualification/switching-cost advantage in high-speed AI-grade laminates, where materials must be designed-in and validated. Judged on the evidence, the returns (return on invested capital about 13%, return on equity about 16%) are decent but cyclically inflated by today's pricing, not structurally high — so this is a narrow moat, roughly stable, not a wide and widening one. Base FR-4 remains competitive and substitutable.

**Secular threat: none / manageable.** There is no structural force eroding the terminal value here — quite the opposite. CCL is essential to every PCB, and artificial-intelligence hardware is a demand tailwind, not a displacement threat. The risk is cyclical (a price and capacity cycle), not secular (a melting business). That distinction matters: the cheapness-versus-history that will eventually appear in this name, if prices roll over, would be a genuine cyclical fear-print to revisit — but today's price is a *rich* print on peak earnings, so the value opportunity is not here yet.

Uniquely among its peers it also makes its own raw materials: the electronic glass yarn, the woven glass cloth, the copper foil and the resin. Full-year 2025 revenue was HK$20.40 billion, up 10%, with net profit of HK$2.44 billion, up 83%, and earnings of HK$0.78 per share. On 30 July 2026 the company published a profit alert guiding first-half 2026 profit above HK$2.8 billion, more than triple the HK$933 million of the first half of 2025, attributing it to continued shortage across CCL and the upstream materials, broad-based price rises, and its vertical integration. It has issued six price-increase letters in 2026, the last two only twenty days apart. If even half of that arrives, the shares at HK$30.00 are being priced at a low-single-digit multiple of 2027 earnings. The balance sheet supports the wait: net debt of about HK$1.75 billion against HK$16.3 billion of equity, a solvency score of 10.1 and a quality score of 7 of 9. The conditions the bull case needs are specific and testable: low-dielectric glass yarn must stay short into 2028 (furnace lead times of eighteen to twenty-four months and slow customer qualification make this plausible); the artificial-intelligence board build-out must not pause; the price letters must keep sticking; and the 24 August half-year results must confirm that the reported profit is now converting into cash rather than into receivables.
bear_thesis: The bear case is that this is a commodity materials company at the top of a violent price cycle, and that the people who know it best have already sold. Three pieces of evidence carry the argument. First, the history. This exact business earned HK$6.78 billion in 2021 on this exact kind of shortage, and HK$907 million two years later - an 87% collapse - accompanied at the time by the same language about structural scarcity being used today. Revenue fell from HK$28.8 billion in 2021 to HK$16.75 billion in 2023. The base rate for 'this time the shortage is structural' in copper-clad laminate is poor, and the capacity answer is already visible: leading board makers are committing billions to new artificial-intelligence board lines landing between 2026 and 2028, and upstream copper foil in China already carries roughly 1.8 million tonnes of capacity against about 1.15 million tonnes of demand, running below 65% utilisation. Second, the insider evidence. The controlling family sold about HK$14.5 billion of stock in 2026 - roughly HK$2.73 billion in March near HK$21, then 155 million shares on 17 June at HK$76.00, an 11.5% discount to the prior close, raising HK$11.78 billion, eight days before the shares peaked at HK$107.20. The stake fell from about 66.6% to 61.7%, and an executive director sold a further million shares on 20 July. The proceeds are being redeployed at the parent, Kingboard Holdings, not in the listed company. Third, and least discussed, the earnings quality. In 2025 the company reported HK$2.44 billion of net profit and generated negative free cash flow of about HK$75 million: operating cash flow of only HK$1.20 billion because receivables absorbed HK$1.83 billion, against HK$1.28 billion of capital spending. It nonetheless paid HK$1.93 billion of dividends, nearly four times the prior year, funded with about HK$868 million of new borrowing. Layer on the disclosure deficit (no earnings calls, no guidance, semi-annual reporting) and the related-party question raised repeatedly in the Hong Kong press through late July, and you have a business whose reported profits are real but whose valuation rests entirely on spot prices that the company itself will not forecast. What confirms the bear: any month in which the price-increase letters stop; a half-year cash-flow statement on 24 August showing another receivables build; or the first sign that low-dielectric yarn capacity additions have been qualified by customers.

The bullish street case, of which Citigroup's 24 July note is the clearest published example, argues the shares are on 8 to 9 times earnings against a low-double-digit historical average and are therefore mispriced, with 2026-28 net-profit forecasts of HK$9.6 billion, HK$14.3 billion and HK$19.5 billion supporting a HK$130 target. Two assumptions inside that are, in our view, factually strained. The first is that a historical average multiple is the right yardstick at this point in the cycle. For a commodity materials company, a trailing multiple averaging low double digits across a full cycle necessarily means the market pays well ABOVE that at the trough and well BELOW it at the peak - so a single-digit multiple on peak earnings is not evidence of cheapness, it is the normal price of peak earnings. The second strained assumption is the 2027 forecast of HK$14.3 billion, which requires spot laminate and glass-cloth prices not merely to hold but to keep climbing through a period in which the industry's own capacity additions arrive - leading board makers are committing billions to new artificial-intelligence lines landing 2026 to 2028, and upstream copper foil in China already runs below 65% utilisation on about 1.8 million tonnes of capacity against roughly 1.15 million tonnes of demand. interrogator_dossier:
# Kingboard Laminates Holdings (HKEX: 1888) - Forensic Dossier

*Prepared 3 August 2026. Price used throughout: HK$30.00, the Hong Kong close on 3 August 2026 (source: live market quote). All figures in Hong Kong dollars unless stated.*

**A note on sources before we begin.** Kingboard Laminates does not hold public earnings calls, and no earnings-call transcript exists for this company in any of the databases available to this committee. There is therefore nothing to quote. This dossier is built instead from what the company actually files and says in writing - its audited annual figures, its stock-exchange announcements (including the profit warning-style "positive profit alert" of 30 July 2026 and the board-meeting notice of 27 July 2026), the disclosure filings covering the controlling family's share sales, and dated broker commentary. Where a normal dossier would test management's spoken narrative against the numbers, here we test the company's *written* narrative and its *actions* against the numbers. That turns out to be more than enough.

---

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

Kingboard Laminates makes copper-clad laminate, or CCL - the fibreglass-and-copper sheet that every printed circuit board is built from. It has been the largest maker of rigid CCL in the world for twenty consecutive years, and unusually it also makes its own raw materials: the electronic glass yarn, the woven glass cloth, the copper foil and the resin chemicals that go into the sheet. That vertical integration is the whole company in one sentence, and it is the reason the last eighteen months happened.

**The story from 2022 to 2025 was survival, not growth.** Revenue fell from HK$28.8 billion in 2021 to HK$16.75 billion in 2023, and net profit collapsed from HK$6.78 billion to HK$907 million - an 87% earnings wipe-out in two years as the post-pandemic electronics glut worked through. There was no narrative to speak of; the company simply kept its factories running and cut its dividend from HK$1.09 billion in 2023 to HK$499 million in 2024.

**From late 2025 the story changed completely, and the change was driven by price, not volume.** Artificial-intelligence servers and switches need far more circuit-board material per box, and they need a *harder* kind of material - low-loss, high-speed laminate built on specialised low-dielectric glass yarn that only a handful of plants in the world can make. That yarn went into genuine shortage. By early June 2026 the common grades of electronic glass cloth had been through five price increases inside the year, reaching about RMB 7.4 per metre - roughly double the low set in the third quarter of 2025 - with Chinese producers running above 100% of nameplate capacity. Kingboard, sitting on its own yarn and cloth capacity, was the single biggest beneficiary in the chain.

**The company's public narrative through 2026 has been conducted almost entirely through price-increase letters.** By mid-July it had issued its sixth price rise of the year, the last one only twenty days after the previous one. On 30 July it published a positive profit alert telling the market that first-half 2026 profit would exceed HK$2.8 billion, more than triple the HK$933 million of the first half of 2025, and attributing the jump explicitly to "continued supply shortage" across CCL and the upstream materials, to broad-based unit price increases, and to its "strong and complete vertical integration."

**What was quietly dropped:** nothing was dropped, because there was never much of a forward narrative to drop. This is the important structural observation about Kingboard Laminates. It gives no earnings guidance, holds no analyst calls, and reports only twice a year. The story you are asked to buy in 2026 is not a story management told you - it is a story the sell-side built out of spot price data and the company's own price letters. That distinction matters enormously when you are deciding what the shares are worth.

---

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

The company makes few explicit claims, so the test here is whether the reported numbers actually support the picture the market has drawn.

| Claim / market belief | What the financials show | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| "Prices are rising sharply and profits are inflecting" | First-half 2026 profit guided above HK$2.8 billion vs HK$933 million a year earlier. Full-year 2025 already showed the turn: revenue HK$20.40 billion (+10%), net profit HK$2.44 billion (+83%), earnings per share HK$0.78. | **Supported.** The inflection is real and large. |
| "Margins are expanding" | Gross margin 19.6% in 2025 and rising; the second half of 2025 alone earned HK$1.51 billion of profit against HK$933 million in the first half. | **Supported.** |
| "This is a high-quality earnings stream" | Here the story breaks. In 2025 the company reported HK$2.44 billion of net profit but generated **negative free cash flow of about HK$75 million**. Operating cash flow was only HK$1.20 billion because receivables absorbed HK$1.83 billion of cash, and capital spending took HK$1.28 billion. | **Diverges sharply.** |
| "Shareholder returns are funded by the business" | The company paid HK$1.93 billion of dividends in 2025 - nearly four times the prior year - while free cash flow was negative. It funded the gap with roughly HK$868 million of new borrowing. Net debt (borrowings less cash and short-term investments) stood at about HK$1.75 billion at 31 December 2025, up from HK$1.36 billion a year earlier. | **Diverges.** The dividend was borrowed, not earned, in cash terms. |
| "Returns justify a premium rating" | Return on equity 15.6% and return on invested capital 13.1% in 2025 - respectable, but this is the *good* part of the cycle. In the 2023 trough the same business earned HK$907 million on roughly HK$15 billion of equity, a return on equity near 6%. | **Partially supported, but cycle-dependent.** |
| Balance sheet is safe | Altman-Z solvency score 10.1, Piotroski quality score 7 of 9, total debt HK$4.63 billion against HK$2.88 billion of cash and short-term investments. Genuinely conservative. | **Supported.** |

**The receivables point deserves its own paragraph, because it is the single most important forensic finding in this file.** In a genuine, severe shortage - which is exactly what management says it is enjoying - a supplier gains bargaining power. Customers queue up, prepay, and accept shorter payment terms. What actually happened in 2025 is the opposite: revenue rose 10% while trade and other receivables rose from HK$7.14 billion to HK$9.21 billion, a HK$1.83 billion cash outflow. Measured against sales, the company is now carrying roughly 165 days of receivables versus about 140 a year earlier. Either the pricing power is less absolute than the narrative implies, or the company is buying volume by extending credit, or the customer base is under strain. None of those three readings is comfortable, and the accounts do not let us distinguish between them.

One correction to the screener data the committee was handed: it lists trailing-twelve-month free cash flow of HK$1.86 billion. The audited 2025 cash-flow statement shows free cash flow of **negative HK$75 million**. The HK$1.86 billion figure appears to be a stale carry-over of 2024's HK$1.93 billion. Use the audited number.

---

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY

**Rating: Rising - but rising in a way that is measured in press releases, not in conviction.**

With no calls to listen to, the only tonal evidence is the cadence and content of the company's own announcements, and there the confidence is unmistakable. Six price-increase letters in seven months, the last two only twenty days apart, is the corporate equivalent of shouting. The 30 July profit alert is written in the language of a company that believes it holds the whip hand: shortage, price increases, vertical integration.

The tone shift from 2023-24 to 2026 is textbook offensive-from-defensive. In 2024 the company cut its dividend by more than half and paid down HK$1.16 billion of borrowings - defensive housekeeping. In 2025 it raised the dividend nearly fourfold and borrowed to do it, and stepped capital spending up 65% to HK$1.28 billion - offensive.

**But there is a countervailing tonal signal that outweighs all of the above, and it is not verbal.** On 17 June 2026 the controlling shareholder sold 155 million shares - about 4.9% of the company - at HK$76.00, an 11.5% discount to the previous close of HK$85.90, raising HK$11.78 billion. That was eight days before the shares peaked at HK$107.20. It followed a first sale in March 2026 of 130 million shares raising about HK$2.73 billion, at roughly HK$21. On 20 July an executive director sold a further one million shares. When the people who see the order book, the price letters and the capacity pipeline before anyone else sell HK$14.5 billion of stock into the top of a move, the confidence expressed in the press releases and the confidence expressed by the cheque book are pointing in opposite directions. The cheque book is the more reliable signal.

---

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY

**Reliability score: Medium - and unrateable in the ordinary sense, because the company does not give guidance.**

Kingboard Laminates issues no revenue or earnings targets, holds no calls, and reports semi-annually. There is therefore no track record of promises kept or broken to score. What we can score is the one forward statement it does make - the profit alert - and one dated market expectation against it.

On 24 July 2026, Citigroup published a note arguing the sell-off was excessive, observing the shares were on 8 to 9 times earnings against a low-double-digit historical average, and forecasting first-half 2026 net profit of about **HK$4.0 billion**, up more than threefold.

On 30 July 2026, the company's own profit alert set the floor at **above HK$2.8 billion**, up more than 200%.

Hong Kong profit alerts are conventionally conservative - "not less than" is the operative sense - so the final number will land above HK$2.8 billion. But a company tracking toward HK$4.0 billion would ordinarily have anchored the alert nearer that level. The market read it as a shortfall against the bull case: the shares fell 7.6% on 30 July to HK$29.14, and the following session traded 205 million shares, the heaviest volume of the entire collapse.

**The pattern to record for the director:** this is a company whose realised numbers have been *spectacular* and whose disclosed forward information is *thin*. That combination is what allowed a 557% share-price advance in under six months and a 73% give-back in six weeks. It is not a fraud signal. It is a volatility signal, and it means the committee cannot lean on management's word for the shape of the second half.

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS

With no question-and-answer sessions, "deflection" is structural rather than tactical - but the unaddressed questions are identifiable, because the market has been asking them loudly in print since late June.

1. **Where are we in the cycle?** The bear argument published widely from mid-July is specific: leading board makers are committing billions to new AI circuit-board lines arriving between 2026 and 2028, and the upstream copper-foil industry in China already carries about 1.8 million tonnes of capacity against roughly 1.15 million tonnes of demand, running below 65% utilisation. The company has said nothing about supply-demand beyond 2026. It has never had to.
2. **How durable is the price?** Six increase letters in seven months invites the obvious question of what happens when the letters stop. No answer has been offered.
3. **Related-party dealing.** Press commentary through late July repeatedly raised concerns about transactions between Kingboard Laminates and its parent, Kingboard Holdings. The parent said the HK$11.78 billion it raised by selling Laminates shares would go into expanding and upgrading *its own* circuit-board business - that is, capital extracted from the listed subsidiary's valuation and redeployed at the parent. This is disclosed and legal. It is also exactly the governance pattern that earns a Hong Kong subsidiary a permanent valuation discount, and the company has not addressed it.
4. **What the sell-side itself cannot agree on.** Published targets currently span roughly HK$20 to HK$130 per share against a HK$30 price. When professional analysts covering the same company disagree by more than six-fold, the honest conclusion is that nobody has an informational edge on the second half - including us.

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS

**Red flags**

- **The controlling family sold HK$14.5 billion in 2026, most of it at HK$76 within eight days of the all-time high** (March placement about HK$2.73 billion near HK$21; 17 June placement HK$11.78 billion at HK$76, an 11.5% discount). The stake fell from about 66.6% to about 61.7%. An executive director added a one-million-share sale on 20 July. This is the highest-quality negative signal in the file.
- **Reported profit did not turn into cash in 2025.** HK$2.44 billion of net profit, negative HK$75 million of free cash flow, HK$1.83 billion swallowed by receivables.
- **The 2025 dividend was debt-funded** - HK$1.93 billion paid out against negative free cash flow, with about HK$868 million of new borrowing raised.
- **Receivables days stretched by roughly 25 days in the very year the company says it had a shortage.** The pricing-power narrative and the working-capital evidence do not agree.
- **The 30 July profit alert set a floor materially below the most bullish published estimate** for the same period, and the shares fell on it.
- **Structural disclosure deficit** - no calls, no guidance, semi-annual reporting. In a violently reflexive commodity cycle this leaves shareholders flying on spot-price gossip between reports.

**Green flags**

- **The earnings inflection is real and verified by the company in writing** - first-half 2026 profit above HK$2.8 billion versus HK$933 million a year earlier.
- **A genuine, defensible position in the scarcest link of the chain.** Low-dielectric glass yarn and cloth cannot be added quickly; furnaces take eighteen to twenty-four months and qualification is slow. Kingboard owns this capacity rather than buying it.
- **Twenty consecutive years as the world's largest rigid-CCL producer** - the scale position is not in dispute.
- **A conservative balance sheet through the whole ordeal.** Net debt of about HK$1.75 billion against HK$16.3 billion of equity, an Altman-Z solvency score of 10.1, and a quality score of 7 of 9. Whatever happens to the cycle, solvency is not the question here.
- **The capital-spending step-up in 2025 was into the products that are actually short**, not into commodity capacity.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS

**The parent company is the tell.** Kingboard Holdings (HKEX: 0148) owns about 61.7% of Kingboard Laminates. At today's prices that stake alone is worth roughly HK$58 billion, while the whole of Kingboard Holdings is capitalised at about HK$46 billion - a 21% discount to just one of its assets. Two readings are possible: Hong Kong is applying its usual holding-company discount, or the market is quietly saying it does not believe the HK$94 billion valuation on the subsidiary. Both readings have been available all year; the discount widened as the subsidiary's price collapsed, which is the more revealing of the two.

**The vocabulary shifted from "laminates" to "upstream."** The 30 July alert leads on glass yarn, glass cloth and copper foil before it mentions CCL. That is management telling you, correctly, that the abnormal profit currently sits in the raw materials, not in the laminate itself. It is also, unintentionally, telling you where the profit will disappear from first: raw-material spreads are the most violently mean-reverting part of this chain, and commodity copper foil is already in structural surplus.

**A small share issue slipped through in 2025** - the share count rose from 3.120 billion to about 3.141 billion, with HK$120 million of stock issued. Immaterial to value, but worth noting that the count is not fixed.

**The 3 August session itself is a signal worth logging.** The shares made a fresh low of HK$26.48 intraday and closed at HK$30.00, up 2.0%, on 103 million shares - a reversal day following the heaviest-volume session of the decline on 31 July. That is what capitulation typically looks like on a chart. It is not, by itself, evidence about the business.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

**Trajectory: STRENGTHENING.** The operating business is inflecting hard and the inflection is confirmed in writing by the company. Profit for the first half of 2026 will be more than triple the prior year. Nothing in this dossier disputes that.

**The single most important thing to weigh before sizing:** you are not being asked whether the earnings are going up. They are. You are being asked *what multiple to pay for earnings that the controlling shareholder valued highly enough to sell HK$11.78 billion of stock into, at a discount, eight days before the top.* Every number in the bull case is a spot-price number. This company earned HK$6.78 billion in 2021 on exactly this kind of shortage and HK$907 million two years later - an 87% collapse. The 2021 episode was accompanied by the same language about structural shortage that is being used today. The base rate for "this time the shortage is structural" in copper-clad laminate is poor, and the family that has run the business through four of these cycles has just voted with HK$14.5 billion.

**Economic moat: NARROW, and stable rather than widening.** The moat type is scale-cost, deepened by vertical integration into a genuinely scarce input (low-dielectric glass yarn and cloth). It is real - twenty years of global leadership is not luck, and the balance sheet lets the company keep investing when competitors cannot. But the width test is what the returns do at the bottom, not the top, and at the bottom this business earns a return on equity near 6%. Today's expanding gross margin is a *price* effect, not a structural one; competitors are adding capacity into it. A cyclical margin spike is not evidence of a widening moat, and this dossier declines to score it as one.

**Secular threat: manageable.** No structural force is eating this company's terminal value. Artificial-intelligence demand is a tailwind for circuit-board materials, not a displacement risk, and there is no substitution technology on the horizon for glass-reinforced laminate in high-layer-count boards. The risk here is cyclical overcapacity, which is a different and far more survivable animal than secular decline. The cheapness question, therefore, is not "value trap versus fear-print" in the terminal sense - it is the narrower and more answerable question of whether the earnings you are capitalising are sustainable or spot. On the evidence, they are substantially spot.
